Name: [ Tray content ] Verify the event-created tray item shows community avatar, title, event-type chip, start date and time, and unseen state
Description: Core content of the enriched event-created tray item (5-element spec). Icon = community avatar (not user avatar / not event thumbnail).
Preconditions:
- A community exists with an avatar set
- The signed-in user is an active, non-banned member of that community
- The Notification Tray is open on the target device
Steps:
1. Have a moderator create a new event in the community
2. Open the Notification Tray on the recipient device
3. Locate the newly created event item
Expected Results:
- The item icon is the COMMUNITY avatar (not the creator/user avatar and not an event thumbnail)
- The primary line reads "[Community name] has event [Event name]"
- The secondary line shows an event-type chip followed by the event start date and start time
- The item is marked as unseen (unseen / primary-tint indicator)

Name: [ Tray content — deleted event ] Verify the tray item keeps the COMMUNITY avatar after its event is deleted
Description: Sibling of [ Tray content ] — same 5-element spec, but exercised AFTER the event is deleted (isDeleted = true). BUG-I: on web-desktop & mobile-web the item icon swaps to a DIFFERENT avatar once the event is deleted (no longer the community avatar). Distinct from [ Deleted event ] (Navigation), which checks the tap destination, not how the item itself renders.
Preconditions:
- An event-created tray item is visible and correctly shows the COMMUNITY avatar
- The signed-in user is an active, non-banned member of that community
- A moderator can delete the event
Steps:
1. Confirm the fresh event item shows the community avatar as its icon
2. Have a moderator delete the event (isDeleted = true)
3. Refresh / re-open the Notification Tray
4. Re-locate the same event item and inspect its icon
Expected Results:
- The item icon is STILL the COMMUNITY avatar — identical to before the deletion
- The icon is NOT swapped to the creator/user avatar, the event thumbnail, or any other image
- The rest of the item content (title, chip, date/time) remains as specified
- Known risk (BUG-I, web-desktop & mobile-web): after deletion the item shows a DIFFERENT avatar — that swap must FAIL this case

Name: [ Event type chip ] Verify the In-person and Virtual chips show the correct label and stay legible in light and dark theme
Description: TR-CL-21 / DEC-05 (expected = legible in both themes, per-platform divergence accepted) + BUG-D (Android chip white-on-white in LIGHT theme). Virtual == livestream (no third chip state).
Preconditions:
- A test community is available for creating both In-person and Virtual (livestream) events
- The target device/app supports both light and dark theme
Steps:
1. Create an In-person event and open its tray item
2. Create a Virtual / livestream event and open its tray item
3. View each item in LIGHT theme
4. View each item in DARK theme
Expected Results:
- The In-person event shows a chip labelled "In-person"
- The Virtual / livestream event shows a chip labelled "Virtual" (there is no third chip type)
- The chip text is legible (sufficient contrast) in LIGHT theme on every platform
- The chip text is legible in DARK theme on every platform
- Known risk (BUG-D): on Android the chip may render white-on-white in light theme — this must FAIL the legibility check

Name: [ Start time timezone ] Verify the tray date and time render in the viewer's local timezone (matching event cards and event detail)
Description: TR-CL-05 REVERSED 2026-07-21 (PM, after dev input): the tray follows existing UIKit behavior and shows the start time in the VIEWER's LOCAL timezone — same as event cards / event detail pages — NOT the event's own timezone. BUG-B1 is therefore RETRACTED: device-local is the intended behavior.
Preconditions:
- Create an event and, in the timezone picker (shown as a GMT offset), select GMT-5 (e.g. New York / Eastern); set the start time to 7:00 PM on 10 Jul 2026
- Set the viewer's device timezone to GMT+7 (e.g. Bangkok)
Steps:
1. Create the GMT-5 event as described
2. On the GMT+7 device, open the event-created tray item
3. Compare with the same event's start time on the event card / event detail page
Expected Results:
- The tray shows the start time converted to the VIEWER's local (GMT+7) timezone — i.e. 7:00 AM on 11 Jul 2026
- This matches how the same event's start time is shown on the event card and the event detail page (all viewer-local)
- It does NOT show the event's source-timezone wall-clock (must NOT show 7:00 PM on 10 Jul)

Name: [ Timestamp & separator ] Verify the relative notification timestamp renders and the date/time has no middle-dot separator
Description: TR-CL-19 (relative timestamp is tray chrome) + TR-CL-18 (no '·' separator — the PRD copy with a dot is wrong).
Preconditions: - An event-created tray item is visible
Steps:
1. Observe the item's notification timestamp (corner / top)
2. Observe the secondary line between the date and the time
Expected Results:
- A relative timestamp is shown (e.g. Just now / 2m / 10h / a date)
- There is NO '·' middle-dot separator between the date and the time
- Date and time are separated by spacing only (per current design, not the PRD copy)

Name: [ Avatar fallback & truncation ] Verify the community-avatar fallback and long-name handling per platform
Description: TR-CL-15. Per-platform truncation differs and is accepted (Web/iOS wrap; Android ellipsizes ~3 lines).
Preconditions:
- A community with NO avatar set
- A community and event with very long names
Steps:
1. Trigger a tray item for the community that has no avatar
2. Trigger a tray item with very long community and event names
Expected Results:
- The no-avatar community shows a fallback (Web = community glyph, iOS = initials, Android = placeholder) — never a broken/empty icon
- Long names do not break the layout or overlap other elements
- Truncation may differ per platform (Web/iOS wrap; Android ellipsizes ~3 lines) — accepted as long as readable

Name: [ Public audience ] Verify a public-community event notifies the entire network including non-members, with no duplicate item
Description: AC-04 network-wide incl non-members (DEC-03) + TR-CL-14 dedup (UNION → 1 item). Needs >=3 accounts.
Preconditions:
- A PUBLIC community
- Account A = active member of that community
- Account B = active network user who is NOT a member of that community
- Account C = the event creator
Steps:
1. As Account C, create an event in the public community
2. Open the tray on Account A (member)
3. Open the tray on Account B (non-member network user)
4. Check Account A for duplicate items
Expected Results:
- Account A (member) receives ONE event-created tray item
- Account B (non-member network user) ALSO receives the item, with the same content (community name shown even though B is not a member)
- Account A sees only ONE item (a member who is also in the network is de-duplicated, not shown twice)
- The creator (Account C) does NOT receive an item for their own event

Name: [ Private audience ] Verify a private-community event notifies only active, non-banned members
Description: AC-05. Private = members-only; non-members and banned members excluded.
Preconditions:
- A PRIVATE community
- Account A = active member
- Account B = network user who is NOT a member
- Account D = a member who is community-banned
Steps:
1. Create an event in the private community
2. Open the tray on Account A (member)
3. Open the tray on Account B (non-member)
4. Open the tray on Account D (banned member)
Expected Results:
- Account A (active member) receives the item
- Account B (non-member) does NOT receive the item
- Account D (banned member) does NOT receive the item
- The creator does not receive their own item

Name: [ Exclusions ] Verify creator, banned, and blocked users are excluded at send and hidden at read
Description: TR-CL-08 creator + TR-CL-17 ban/leave after receive (hide at read, node kept) + TR-CL-24 user-block bidirectional.
Preconditions:
- An event created in a community
- A recipient who will be banned after receiving
- A recipient who has a block relationship with the creator (either direction)
Steps:
1. Create the event and confirm eligible members received the item
2. Ban a recipient (global or community) and re-open their tray
3. Set up a block between a recipient and the creator, then create another event
Expected Results:
- The creator never receives their own event item
- A user banned AFTER receiving no longer sees the item on next read (hidden at read; node not deleted)
- Un-banning / re-joining within retention restores visibility
- If the recipient and creator have a block relationship (either direction), the item is suppressed

Name: [ Block after notify ] Verify blocking after a notification was delivered blocks the recipient's access on tap
Description: TR-CL-29 Scenario A / DEC-08 (new scope, blocking extended to events, bidirectional). Different timing than [ Exclusions ], which covers a block made BEFORE the event is created.
Preconditions:
- User A and User B are not blocked
- User A creates an event in a shared community and User B receives the event-created tray item
- User A then blocks User B (or User B blocks User A)
Steps:
1. As User B, open the Notification Tray
2. Tap the event's tray item that was received before the block
Expected Results: - User B lands on a no-access state, even though the notification was delivered before the block existed

Name: [ Late join ] Verify a user who joins a private community after an event is created does not receive that event's notification
Description: TR-CL-23 — private community gives no retroactive backfill to a user who joins after the event was created.
Preconditions:
- A PRIVATE community already has an event, and its event-created tray item was delivered to the members who were in the community at that time
- A separate test user is NOT yet a member of that community
Steps:
1. Have the test user join the private community (after the event was created)
2. Open that user's Notification Tray
Expected Results:
- The newly joined user does NOT receive the earlier event's tray item
- Only members who were in the community when the event was created received it (no retroactive backfill)

Name: [ Privacy change ] Verify switching a community to private keeps notifications already sent and guards access on tap
Description: TR-CL-16 / FU-4 — audience is a send-time snapshot (no recompute on privacy change); public->private exposure is handled by the nav/permission guard (event getById returns 403 for a non-member).
Preconditions:
- A PUBLIC community created an event, so its tray item was delivered network-wide (including to non-members)
- A non-member who received that item is signed in on the target device
Steps:
1. Switch the community from public to private
2. Open the non-member's Notification Tray
3. As that non-member, tap the event's tray item
Expected Results:
- The already-delivered tray item is NOT removed after the privacy change (audience is a snapshot at send time)
- Tapping the now-private event is blocked — the event shows as unavailable and the non-member is not let in

Name: [ Tray tap ] Verify tapping an event-created tray item opens the event detail page with RSVP visible
Description: TR-CL-01 / FU-1. Destination = event detail page (RSVP CTA already visible there), not a separate RSVP page. Push reuses this same nav.
Preconditions: - An event-created tray item is visible and the event still exists
Steps: 1. Tap the event-created tray item
Expected Results:
- The event detail page opens
- The RSVP action / button is visible on that page
- This is the shared destination that a push tap also routes to once wired

Name: [ Deleted event ] Verify tapping a tray item for a deleted event shows a graceful unavailable state with no crash or blank
Description: TR-CL-03 + BUG-C (Android shows 'This community is private' for a DELETED event) + BUG-E (web FailedToShow flash on load). iOS conflates deleted vs forbidden.
Preconditions: - An event-created tray item whose event is then deleted (isDeleted = true) before tapping
Steps:
1. Delete the event
2. Tap the tray item for the deleted event
Expected Results:
- A graceful 'no longer available' state is shown — no crash, no error, no blank screen
- A Go-back / dismiss path is available
- Known risk (BUG-C, Android): a deleted event must NOT say 'This community is private' — that wrong message must FAIL
- Known risk (BUG-E, web): the unavailable screen must not flash before the content finishes loading

Name: [ Left community ] Verify a former member tapping the event notification after leaving sees it as no longer available
Description: TR-CL-27. Same nav-guard family as [ Privacy change ], triggered by the member leaving rather than a privacy flip.
Preconditions:
- A member of a PRIVATE community received an event-created tray item
- That member then leaves the private community
Steps:
1. As the former member, open the Notification Tray or the original notification
2. Tap the event's tray item
Expected Results:
- The event shows as no longer available
- The former member is not let into the private community's event

Name: [ Event ended ] Verify tapping a notification for an ended event opens Event Detail with no RSVP button
Description: TR-CL-28. Contrast with [ Deleted event ]: an ended event still exists and opens normally, it just no longer offers RSVP — it does NOT show an 'unavailable' state.
Preconditions: - An event-created tray item exists for an event whose scheduled time has already passed (the event has ended)
Steps: 1. Tap the event's tray item
Expected Results:
- The Event Detail page opens (not an 'unavailable' state)
- The page shows an ended state
- No RSVP button is shown

Name: [ No grouping ] Verify each event creation produces its own distinct tray item
Description: TR-CL-04 — no grouping, even for multiple events from the same community.
Preconditions: - One community that will host multiple events
Steps:
1. Create 3 events in the same community
2. Open the tray
Expected Results:
- Each event appears as its OWN separate tray item
- Items are NOT grouped or collapsed even when they come from the same community

Name: [ Unseen & seen ] Verify the unseen indicator is computed correctly and clears only on mark-seen, not on fetch
Description: AC-01 unseen + TR-CL-06 (client computes lastTrayOccurredAt > lastTraySeenAt; seen set by markTraySeen/markItemsSeen only; fetch does not set seen).
Preconditions: - A fresh event-created tray item that has never been seen
Steps:
1. Fetch / load the tray list without triggering the mark-seen action
2. Trigger the seen action (open tray / mark seen per platform)
3. Re-open the tray
Expected Results:
- A new item appears as unseen
- Merely fetching the list does not by itself flip the item to seen if mark-seen is not triggered
- After mark-seen, the item shows as seen and the unseen count decreases

Name: [ Event edited ] Verify editing an event updates its existing tray item (live, not a snapshot)
Description: TR-CL-12 — serializer re-fetches the event at read; edit reflects after the short Redis cache TTL.
Preconditions: - An event-created tray item exists
Steps:
1. Edit the event's name / time / type
2. Wait for the cache TTL to expire
3. Re-open the tray item
Expected Results:
- The tray item reflects the UPDATED event details (name / time / type)
- It is not frozen to the values at creation time (live re-fetch, not a snapshot)

Name: [ Backfill & old format ] Verify pre-existing items get the new content at read and network broadcast stays forward-only
Description: TR-CL-13, CONFIRMED by PM via TR-CL-30 (2026-07-22, answer C): an old event (created before this release) shows the new rich content when reopened, but does not newly start reaching the whole network.
Preconditions:
- An event exists that was created before this release, in a community (its tray item still shows the old content, e.g. "You've been invited to an event")
- A second test account is a network user who is NOT a member of that community
Steps:
1. As a member of that community, open the old event's tray item
2. As the second account (non-member of that community), check whether the same tray item appears
Expected Results:
- The member sees the old item now showing the new content (community avatar, chip, start date, start time) — not the old generic text
- The non-member does NOT see that item — it has not started reaching the whole network

Name: [ Console toggle ] Verify the event-creation push toggle is present and correctly labelled
Description: PDT-3676 AC-01. Toggle = event-activate-switch (field isPushNotifiable) under the 'Event-related events' section.
Preconditions:
- The signed-in account is a network admin with Admin Console access
- Push notifications are enabled for the network
Steps:
1. Open Admin Console → Settings → Push notifications
2. Open the Community tab / 'Event-related events' section
Expected Results:
- A section titled 'Event-related events' is present
- It contains a toggle labelled 'When someone creates a new event in the community'
- The toggle sits alongside the 'event reminder' and 'event started' toggles

Name: [ Toggle on ] Verify enabling the toggle sends a push to community members and deep-links to the event
Description: PDT-3676 AC-03 + P-CL-2 (members only, not network-wide). Combines list #1 (enable) with delivery.
Preconditions:
- The 'When someone creates a new event in the community' toggle is OFF
- Account A is an active, non-banned member of the community (push enabled)
- Account B is a network user who is not a member of the community (push enabled)
Steps:
1. Turn the toggle ON and save
2. Create a new event in a PUBLIC community as another user
3. Observe the push on Account A (member)
4. Observe the push on Account B (non-member)
Expected Results:
- The toggle switches to ON and the setting persists
- Account A (member) receives an event-creation push
- Account B (non-member) does NOT receive the push — audience is community members only, even for a public community (unlike the tray)
- Tapping the push deep-links to the event (once push-tap is wired in the host app)

Name: [ Toggle off ] Verify disabling the toggle stops the push while the in-app tray still fires
Description: PDT-3676 AC-02 + list #2. Cross-surface: push and tray are independent.
Preconditions:
- The 'When someone creates a new event in the community' toggle is ON
- A member device with push enabled
Steps:
1. Turn the toggle OFF and save
2. Create a new event in the community
3. Observe the member device for a push
4. Open the member's in-app notification tray
Expected Results:
- The toggle switches to OFF and the setting persists
- No event-creation push is delivered
- The in-app tray item still appears to community members (the tray is independent of the push toggle)

Name: [ Edit message ] Verify the push message template can be edited, placeholders inserted, and saved
Description: Beyond PDT-3676 AC — the console 'Edit message for event' modal (Notification Title + Notification Text + placeholder buttons). Merges list #3, #4, #5, #6.
Preconditions:
- The signed-in account can edit push-notification settings
- The 'Event-related events' list is visible
Steps:
1. Click the edit (pencil) icon in the Actions column for the event-creation row
2. Replace the Notification Title with e.g. 'New event in {{CommunityName}}!'
3. Replace the Notification Text with e.g. '{{EventName}} starts on {{EventStartDate}}'
4. Place the cursor in a field and click a placeholder button e.g. {{EventType}}
5. Click OK / Save
Expected Results:
- The 'Edit message for event' modal opens showing the current Notification Title, Notification Text, and the list of supported placeholders
- Clicking a placeholder button inserts that placeholder at the cursor position
- On save, the edited title and text persist
- A newly created event's push reflects the edited title and body, with placeholders replaced by real values

Name: [ Message validation ] Verify the title and text length limits and empty-field handling
Description: Beyond PDT-3676 AC. Title limit 62, Text limit 235, empty-field block. Merges list #7, #8, #9.
Preconditions: - The 'Edit message for event' modal is open
Steps:
1. Type more than 62 characters in the Notification Title field
2. Type more than 235 characters in the Notification Text field
3. Clear the Title and/or Text field to leave it empty
4. Click OK / Save
Expected Results:
- The Title field does not accept more than 62 characters; its counter (x/62) updates correctly
- The Text field does not accept more than 235 characters; its counter (x/235) updates correctly
- An empty Title or Text shows a validation error and is not saved

Name: [ Modal controls ] Verify Restore Default reverts and Cancel or X discards changes
Description: Beyond PDT-3676 AC. Merges list #10, #11, #12.
Preconditions: - The 'Edit message for event' modal is open with the title/text edited but not yet saved
Steps:
1. Click 'Restore Default'
2. Edit the fields again, then click 'Cancel'
3. Reopen the modal, edit the fields, then click the X (top-right)
Expected Results:
- 'Restore Default' reverts the Notification Title and Text to the system's original default values
- 'Cancel' closes the modal without saving — reopening shows the pre-edit text
- The X button closes the modal without saving

Name: [ Template rendering ] Verify saved placeholders and emoji render as real values in the delivered push
Description: Beyond PDT-3676 AC. Merges list #13, #14 — verifies the console edit produces correct push output.
Preconditions:
- The push message template is edited to include all placeholders and an emoji / special characters, and saved
- The toggle is ON
- A member device (iOS / Android) with push enabled
Steps:
1. Create an event named 'Yoga Night' in the community 'Fitness Club', type virtual, starting 21 Jul 2026 18:00
2. Observe the delivered push on the member device
Expected Results:
- The push replaces {{CommunityName}} with 'Fitness Club', {{EventName}} with 'Yoga Night', and fills {{EventType}}, {{EventStartDate}}, {{EventStartTime}} with the real event values
- Emoji and special characters display correctly with no encoding issues
- The start date/time render in the viewer's device-local timezone (consistent with the tray; verified on Android + iOS)

Name: [ Access control ] Verify push-notification settings are restricted by role
Description: Beyond PDT-3676 AC. List #16.
Preconditions: - The signed-in account has a role that lacks access to the push-notification settings
Steps:
1. Attempt to open the Push notifications settings page
2. Attempt to edit the event-creation toggle or message
Expected Results:
- Access is denied or a permission-denied message is shown, per the role's permissions
- An unauthorized role cannot change the setting or the message

Name: [ Push content ] Verify the push shows the correct title, body chip and date/time, and community-avatar icon
Description: PDT-3677 AC-05. OS notification text is server-rendered. Icon = community avatar.
Preconditions:
- The event-creation push toggle is ON
- A member device (iOS / Android) with push enabled
Steps:
1. Create an In-person event in the community
2. Observe the push notification on the member device
3. Repeat with a Virtual event
Expected Results:
- The push title reads '[Community name] has event [Event name]'
- The push body shows the event-type chip label ('In-person' or 'Virtual') followed by the start date and start time
- The notification icon is the community avatar
- An event with an unknown type shows an empty chip label ('')

Name: [ Push timezone ] Verify the push start time renders in the viewer's device-local timezone (matching the tray)
Description: Push shows the start time in the VIEWER's device-local timezone — consistent with the tray (DEC-06) and existing UIKit surfaces. VERIFIED CORRECT on Android + iOS (2026-07-21). Supersedes BUG-B2: the earlier source-based 'push renders UTC' inference did not reproduce on device.
Preconditions:
- Create an event and, in the timezone picker (shown as a GMT offset), select GMT-5 (e.g. New York / Eastern); set the start time to 7:00 PM on 10 Jul 2026
- Set the viewer's device timezone to GMT+7 (e.g. Bangkok)
- The event-creation push toggle is ON
Steps:
1. Create the GMT-5 event with the push toggle ON
2. On the GMT+7 device, observe the push notification body
Expected Results:
- The push body shows the start time converted to the viewer's device-local (GMT+7) timezone — i.e. 7:00 AM on 11 Jul 2026
- It matches the in-app tray and event detail (all viewer-local)
- It does NOT show raw UTC (12:00 AM / midnight 11 Jul) nor the event's source-tz wall-clock (7:00 PM 10 Jul)

Name: [ Virtual single push ] Verify a virtual event delivers exactly one push with the Room go-live push suppressed
Description: PDT-3677 AC-04. Dedup is backend-only; no client-side dedup exists.
Preconditions:
- The push toggle is ON
- A member device with push enabled
Steps:
1. Create a VIRTUAL event (which auto-generates a Room)
2. Observe all push notifications delivered to the member device
Expected Results:
- Exactly ONE push notification is delivered for the event
- No separate Room / livestream-creation push arrives for the same event (it is suppressed)

Name: [ OS opt-out ] Verify a device or OS push opt-out stops the push but not the in-app tray
Description: PDT-3677 AC-03. push and tray are independent.
Preconditions:
- A member has disabled push for the app at the device / OS level
- The push toggle is ON at network level
Steps:
1. Disable push for the app in device / OS settings
2. Create an event in the community
3. Observe the device for a push
4. Open the in-app notification tray
Expected Results:
- No push is delivered (the OS suppresses it)
- The in-app tray item still appears (the tray is independent of the OS push opt-out)

Name: [ Push tap ] Verify tapping the push opens the event detail / RSVP page
Description: PDT-3677 AC-01 + P-CL-8: push-tap routing is host-app/integrator responsibility (not wired in the reference sample apps). Destination nav is the SAME as the tray tap. Run on a push-integrated host build.
Preconditions:
- A push-integrated host app that routes the event.created payload (eventId) to the UIKit event detail page
- An event-creation push has been received
Steps: 1. Tap the received event-creation push
Expected Results:
- The event detail / RSVP page for that event opens (routed off the eventId payload)
- The RSVP action is visible
- If the host app does not wire push-tap routing, this cannot be verified on that build — the shared destination nav is covered by the Tray tap case

Name: [ Push deleted ] Verify tapping a push for a deleted event shows a graceful unavailable state
Description: PDT-3677 AC-02 + shared BUG-C (Android). Same nav path as the Tray deleted-event case; event getById returns 404.
Preconditions:
- A push-integrated host build
- An event-creation push whose event is deleted before tapping
Steps:
1. Delete the event after the push is delivered
2. Tap the push
Expected Results:
- A graceful 'This event is no longer available' state is shown (event getById returns 404)
- No error or blank screen
- Known risk (BUG-C, Android): must NOT show 'This community is private' for a deleted event

Name: [ Block hides event in Hub ] Verify blocked users don't see each other's events in the Event Hub
Description: TR-CL-29 Scenario C / DEC-08 (new scope). Cross-surface check: validates the same block rule Jack is adding, on the Event Hub / Event tab listing rather than the notification tray.
Preconditions:
- User A and User B are both members of the same community
- User A and User B have a block relationship (either direction)
Steps:
1. As User A, create an event in the shared community
2. As User B, open the Event tab / Event Hub for that community
3. As User A, open the Event tab / Event Hub and look for any event User B created
Expected Results:
- User B does not see User A's event in the Event tab / Event Hub
- User A does not see User B's events either — hidden from each other both ways
